final_candidates.decision_summary: Tryptophan to aspartate at position 17 removes a large aromatic core residue and introduces a charged side chain, severely disrupting hydrophobic packing and likely preventing proper folding.
Phenylalanine to aspartate in the hydrophobic core introduces charge and reduces volume, strongly destabilizing the folded state.
Leucine to proline at position 11 likely disrupts a helical segment, introducing backbone kink and reducing folding stability.

stop_reason.detail: Further self-iteration without external evidence will not meaningfully improve confidence or ranking of top candidates.

history.rationale: Leu11 is likely part of a helical segment; proline will introduce a rigid kink and break helical packing. This should severely disrupt PsaE folding.
Proline at position 11 is likely to disrupt a helix; retention with increased confidence.
Trp17 is a large aromatic residue likely buried in the hydrophobic core; replacement with aspartate removes essential packing and introduces charge. This strongly destabilizes the folded state.
Tryptophan to aspartate is highly disruptive due to loss of aromatic core and introduced charge; top candidate.
Phe40 is an exposed-to-core hydrophobic residue; substituting it with aspartate disrupts the core and creates electrostatic strain. Folding would be highly compromised.
Phenylalanine to aspartate strongly destabilizes the hydrophobic core; top candidate.
Ile10 is a buried hydrophobic residue; a charged aspartate at this site will disrupt local hydrophobicity and likely impair folding. This should knock out functional PsaE.
Isoleucine to aspartate adds charge to a hydrophobic region, likely destabilizing.
Ile33 sits in a hydrophobic patch near the core; introducing aspartate will disrupt core packing. The resulting charge burial is strongly destabilizing.
Isoleucine to aspartate in a hydrophobic cluster; increased confidence.
Leu55 is likely in a C-terminal secondary-structure element; proline will introduce backbone torsion constraints and destabilize that region. This likely prevents proper folding.
Proline may disrupt secondary structure; moderate confidence.
Tyr34 is an aromatic core residue; replacement with aspartate removes aromatic packing and adds charge in a nonpolar environment. This should significantly destabilize the fold.
Tyrosine to aspartate is disruptive due to charge and size change.
Val24 is a likely buried aliphatic residue; replacing it with arginine introduces a large charged side chain into the core. Steric and electrostatic clashes will disrupt folding.
Valine to arginine adds a large charged residue, likely destabilizing.
Phe60 is another core aromatic; aspartate substitution removes hydrophobic content and adds a buried charge. This will impair folding and likely ablate PsaE function.
Phenylalanine to aspartate is disruptive but near C-terminus, lowering confidence.
Ala61 is a small hydrophobic residue; a lysine at this position will introduce a bulky charged side chain, disrupting local packing and stability. Folding should be compromised.
Alanine to lysine is less disruptive, likely surface exposed; rejected.

rejection.reason: Alanine to lysine is less disruptive, likely surface exposed; rejected.

history.rationale: Valine to aspartate at a buried hydrophobic position, expected to destabilize folding.
